brief: Betting markets and polling point to a near-certain Democratic House and a toss-up Senate: Polymarket puts House odds at 92%, Senate at 63%, and the generic ballot shows a Democratic lead of about 8.3 points, wider than in 2022 or 2024. Historically the president's party loses about 27 House and 3 Senate seats per midterm, and 20 of the last 23 midterms cost the incumbent party seats. Even a Democratic sweep would be checked by a Republican White House veto and the Senate filibuster, so sweeping legislation stays unlikely over the next two years; must-pass bills (budget, debt ceiling, defense authorization) remain the real battleground. JPMorgan built three scenario baskets, Gridlock, Blue Wave and Red Wall, covering 125+ stocks: Gridlock caps downside policy risk and favors healthcare and defense; Blue Wave favors hospitals, Medicaid managed care and renewables; Red Wall is most supportive of AI/datacenter buildout, energy and financials deregulation. Six-month basket performance has favored Gridlock (+9%) and Blue Wave (+1%) over Red Wall (-1.5%). Separately, S&P 500 options price only a modest event premium even though the VIX has historically risen into midterms, so JPMorgan favors positioning for higher volatility ahead of the vote.
